clue.text: Sorceress standing by small birch

indicators.note: the sorceress stands next to the small letter, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a sorceress is a witch

explanation.surface: A witch waits beside a little birch tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A birch is a bundle of twigs used for flogging, as is a cane or rod: both are a thin flexible stick for beating.

clue.text: Strong wines drunk, unknown number

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and jumbled, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: in algebra Y is a conventional unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Strong wines have been consumed, an uncounted amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscular and tough, with visible tendons, so physically strong.

clue.text: A pack of hounds may be completely confused, initially, over tracks

definitions.text: A pack of hounds may be

parts.note: to pay in full is to pay completely

indicators.note: only the opening letter of confused is used

parts.note: RY, railway, is a crossword abbreviation for tracks

explanation.surface: A hunting pack may be utterly bewildered, from the start, over the trails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link word: it places the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Hounds that have picked up the scent and give tongue together are said to be baying in this state of full chase.

clue.text: Check on a dazzling display in ceremonial carriage

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
taken as written
a riot of colour is a dazzling display

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a brilliant show inside a ceremonial coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle used in ancient warfare, processions and triumphs.

clue.text: Tea without milk or sugar for minister

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
food or drink served with nothing added is plain

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes his tea black and unsweetened.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman attached to a hospital, regiment or college is a kind of minister of religion.

clue.text: Plant book under author's name

indicators.note: in a down answer the book is written beneath the name, so it comes second

parts.note: Thomas Hardy, the English novelist, gives his surname
an annual is a book published once a year

explanation.surface: A volume filed under its writer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that completes its life cycle in one year and tolerates frost, such as a marigold.

clue.text: Artist's picture — seeing that, what of it?

parts.note: pic is short for picture
as means since or seeing that
'so?' is a dismissive retort meaning what of it

explanation.surface: A painting by an artist, seen and dismissed with a shrug.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso, the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism, is a famous example of an artist.

clue.text: A couple of books on Old Testament religious leader

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits on top of the next, so they run in order

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for book, so two books give BB

explanation.surface: A religious leader keeps two volumes on the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a community of monks is a religious leader.

clue.text: Element of unusual ringtone

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters take an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Part of a strange phone ringtone.
explanation.definitionFit: The gas making up most of the air, chemical symbol N, is an element.

clue.text: Certainly not name of listener

parts.note: taken as written
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Someone flatly refuses to give the name of the person who overheard.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British exclamation of emphatic refusal, like 'not a chance'.

clue.text: Blunt criticism from stalwart that goes to club

parts.note: a dependable, staunch person is informally called a brick
a bat is a club for striking a ball

explanation.surface: Harsh words from a loyal supporter who attends the club.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a piece of brick thrown as a missile, figuratively a harsh, unflattering remark.

clue.text: Heather cuddled by Bill without hesitation

indicators.note: being cuddled means being held inside someone's arms, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Bill and Willy are both pet forms of William
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: Heather is happily hugged by Bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something readily and gladly means acting with no reluctance or pause.

clue.text: Fall from vessel and get carried away?

definitions.meaning: literally to tumble over the side of a ship
idiomatically to behave with excessive enthusiasm

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means falling over a ship's side and figuratively means overdoing something.

clue.text: Argument made by group against

parts.note: a set is a group of things or people
to can mean in contact with or against, as in 'back to back'

explanation.surface: A dispute arises from a group that opposes something.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief fight or heated quarrel is a dust-up, a scrap.

clue.text: Wallpaper may be put in one's place?

definitions.text: Wallpaper may be put in one's place?

parts.words: Wallpaper may be put in one's place?
parts.note: a roll of wallpaper is trimmed to fit the wall, and to humble an arrogant person is to put them in their place

explanation.walkthrough: The decorating sense is literal trimming of paper to fit; the other sense is the idiom for deflating someone's self-importance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to humble someone who has grown conceited, reducing their importance.

clue.text: Rough Irish professional soldier

parts.note: a regular is a soldier of the standing professional army

explanation.surface: A tough, uncouth Irish career soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven and not smooth, like a rough or bumpy surface.

clue.text: Son worrying about rook showing sign of injury

indicators.note: the worrying word goes about, around, the letter

parts.note: caring, as in caring about something, means being concerned or worried
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A boy fretting over a rook that bears a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking the skin with healed wounds is a visible sign that someone was hurt.

clue.text: Blubber's found by obscene killing — complain very loudly

parts.note: to blubber is to cry noisily
blue jokes or films are rude or obscene
murder is unlawful killing

explanation.surface: A weeper reacts to a lewd murder by making a terrible fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to protest loudly and indignantly, often out of proportion to the cause.

clue.text: Framework of room locked up by the Parisian

indicators.note: being locked up means being shut inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: le is French for the
an attic is a room under the roof

explanation.surface: The structure of a loft secured by a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure of crossed strips with gaps between them is a framework or trellis.

clue.text: Uncooperative suspect fainted

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or not genuine, so the letters are not in their true order

explanation.surface: A suspect who passed out, refusing to help police.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who openly resists authority is obstinate and refuses to cooperate.

clue.text: Having an unpleasant smell, writing fluid in pen

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
ink is fluid for writing

explanation.surface: Ink spilled in a fountain pen leaves a foul odour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing pen next to ink, but it is the pigpen.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeking or malodorous, an informal adjective for foul-smelling.

clue.text: Complete shock when female is fired

indicators.note: a fired worker is removed from the firm, so this letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a fright is a sudden shock

explanation.surface: A total shock as a woman loses her job.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British usage: 'a right mess' means a complete or utter mess, so the word works as an intensifying synonym.

clue.text: Unattractively large total before deductions

definitions.meaning: describing something obese or repulsively big
income or profit counted before tax and expenses are subtracted

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both repulsively fat and the whole sum before anything is taken off.

clue.text: Quarrel after religious edict brings one to this Spanish spectacle

indicators.note: the quarrel comes after the edict, so it follows it in the answer

parts.note: a papal bull is an edict issued by the Pope
a fight is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A dispute over a papal decree leads someone to watch a show in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A corrida, the traditional public contest with a matador, is the best-known spectacle of Spain.

clue.text: Press dogged by one caller, not half sarcastic

indicators.note: dogging someone means following behind them, so the other pieces come after

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: only half of the word caller is kept, its first three letters

explanation.surface: A journalist is pursued by a half-hearted caller who mocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the opposite of what is meant with mocking intent is a form of irony, so ironic and scornful overlap.

clue.text: Liquid measure, litre, swallowed by girl, working

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside, so the letter goes into the word

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A girl downs a litre while busy at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of volume for fluids, eight pints, is a standard measure for liquids.

clue.text: Date one person regularly in travel firm

parts.note: to go is to travel
steady means firm or stable

explanation.surface: Someone dates a colleague at the travel company.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes an exclusive romantic relationship, seeing only one partner.

clue.text: Passionate tale gripping millions

indicators.note: the tale holds the letter tight within it

parts.note: a tale is a story
M is the standard abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A romantic story that holds millions of readers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempestuous relationship or temper is full of strong, turbulent feeling.
